key_insight: The paper turns crop-growth and energy-response data into a surrogate-based MILP that optimizes vertical-farm lighting schedules to cut electricity cost while still meeting harvest targets.
engineering_relevance: It provides a tractable optimization workflow for industrial vertical farming that couples crop physiology, energy demand, and electricity-price variability in a single scheduling model.
method: Generate or collect crop-energy data across lighting, crop stage, and temperature conditions.
Fit surrogate relationships for biomass growth, leaf area index, and lighting/heating/cooling demand.
Embed the surrogates in a MILP and test different temporal aggregation levels for accuracy vs. tractability.
evidence_signal: Using synthetic data from a validated agri-energy model for lettuce in an industrial-scale vertical farm, the optimized schedules reduced electricity use by up to 15.9% and cost by up to 17.8% while meeting the target harvest weight.
watch_item: Performance depends on representative training data and validated surrogate ranges; extrapolation outside the sampled crop stages, control settings, or temperature conditions may weaken reliability.
paper_title: From Crop and Energy Data to Optimized Lighting Scheduling: A Surrogate-Based MILP Framework for Vertical Farming
